Road Accident fund runs out of road

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The RAF has run out of road. What can save it and who is at the helm

Unique Selling Point:
All the information in our story is a matter of court record. ITs contentious, its important and its about to fall over and Maponya are prepared to speak to Carte Blanche

Summary:
In the final months of 2020, a flurry of legal action around the RAF was taking place. Attorneys are suing the RAF, the RAF was going to court to prevent the attorneys from removing its furniture, its bank account and even the fuel levy on which it depends, and another firm of former panel attorneys, Maponya prepared lengthy documents to apply to wind up the RAF but put their application on hold till January this year. There were judgements and appeals, but now its 2021 when the rubber will hit the road for the RAF and those in the know say it could implode


Further information:
Every year there are a million accidents, 13 000 deaths and more than 262 000 injures. That translates into 100 000 personal claims against the RAF every year, but only 47% are finalized which means that over 53 000 claims are carried over to the following year. Now add those to the 245 000 claims that are still outstanding, not enough staff to process the claims and some voracious plaintiff attorneys into the mix and its easy to see how an implosion can happen.

And even as lawyers and sheriffs fight the RAF, the RAF itself has taken its own bank to court to prevent it from handing out money when court orders from frustrated attorneys trying to get claims paid for their clients, attach its bank accounts. But there is more – in an application launched by plaintiff attorney Kabelo Malau, he asks the court to find the recent appointment of the new CEO Collins Letsoalo irrational. He sets out clearly the history of Letsoalo at the RTMC and PRASA, and its an unflattering picture. ( Malau wont go on the record but we can find a way to reflect what is in the papers.

In December the RAF managed to get a rule Nisi – an interdict that expires after a certain time frame – to give it 180 days ( 6 months) of breathing room in which no sheriff or plaintiff attorney can attach its bank account or its computers or its chairs. It seems hard to believe but its become almost standard practice for plaintiff attorneys to get a court order to get payment and attach whatever they can if the RAF doesn’t settle their long overdue claims. There are over 5000 attachments pending- speak to PIPLA – the plaintiff attorneys association and they will tell you that at one legal firm alone there is R100 million in writs – just waiting for a window to attach the ABSA bank account.

The urgent application by the CEO of the RAF was granted in November last year, but its not permanent. That case will go back to court next month, but in the meantime – the CEO’s affidavit sets out the train wreck that is the RAF’s financial situation. The CEO says the RAF is insolvent and he highlights very specifically the exact amounts – and they are eye watering. According to the minister and the CEO a massive deficit has worsened dramatically over the past five years. A the end of 2018 it was R26.4 billion, by end 2019 it was R55.8 billion and now they are staring down a R260 billion deficit.

But, Letsoalo tells the courts he has a five year plan to turn the RAF around. Don’t hold your breath, so far no one has managed to pull the RAF right, and the billions it owes now means that the RAF is the second biggest risk to the country’s balance sheet after Eskom. And then there is the pandemic. For every litre of petrol we buy the RAF takes just over R2-00 of that. If you are an average motorist in SA you are paying roughly R400 per month for the benefit of the RAF. But if you are ever a victim of a serious MVA injury, you could wait up to seven years for your money. And lockdown last year didn’t help – they are R7 billion rand down.

Maponya can prove they are owed R20 million rand for work already done, but they say that at the start of lockdown the RAF pulled the rug from under them, and demanded their files. This is part of the new strategy of the CEO – get rid of the panel attorneys that are there to help protect RAF funds from over inflated claims by plaintiff attorney.
Its been almost a year and Maponya’s Baitseng Rangata – chairperson of the board has run out of patience. Their application is ready for the court role. It could be precedent setting, it could be disastrous. The minister who has opposed the application says it is self- serving and incompetent in law, as only parliament can decide what to do with the RAF – not Maponya application using the companies act to liquidate the fund.

So does the RAF have a future in its current form, or is it time to look at another way of doing things? Certainly the way that both the RAF and attorneys are operating has become almost farcical, except that its tragic, because those injured in life changing accidents, the stretched South African motorist, and the fiscus are all the worse off, as long as this sorry saga continues.

Carte Blanche navigates our viewers through this morass, we speak to Maponya, and Professor Hennie Klopper and others, to bring you a crisp and concise overview of a fund that is supposed to be an asset for South Africa but instead has become its second biggest liability after Eskom.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT RAF RUNS OUT ROAD JAN 2021 FOR FINAL MIX TX SUNDAY 31 JAN 2021

Commentary One
Every file in this room represents a life, torn apart by a serious accident on South Africa’s roads

Up sound taxi accident

Commentary Two
We kill and maim each other at an alarming rate. Every year 13 000 people die, another 62 000 are seriously injured. Those that live, hope the Road accident fund will help them rebuild their shattered lives.

LINK
But now the Road accident fund has run out of road, and the CEO has warned that the implosion of the Road Accident fund is imminent- and will have disastrous consequences for the country

Commentary Three
Collins Letsoalo is the new CEO

Collins
Well this implosion will happen if we do nothing, the do nothing scenario is RAF is going to implode, that is why we are saying its not sustainable in its current form

Commentary Four
The RAF already has 310 000 claims overdue, and owes at least R17 billion in settled claims it hasn’t been able to pay

Collins
Most of these claims that we are paying this year, are the ones from five years ago

Commentary Five
And more claims just keep on coming. Professor Hennie Klopper, let’s call him an RAF encyclopedia, explains the snowballing effect.

Hennie
They get in on an annual basis 100 000 claims. Of those 100 000 claims they get in a year, they complete only 28%, which means they carry over 72 000
Masa
Over and above the new claims of that year
Hennie
Ya

Commentary Six
And each claim waiting is a damaged life on hold. In 2014 Chris Karkos was knocked off his motorbike in a hit and run
Chris
and it’s like in a second I was like on the road and paralysed from the neck down – I didn’t hear or see anything and the guy that knocked me, carried on driving off.

Commentary seven
His injuries were extensive

Chris
I broke my femur bones on my right leg, I lost my joints on my right hip, the nerves were basically pulled out of my neck, luckily for me as time went on my hands started coming back, I started getting feeling back in the rest of my body, it’s just my right arm, I completely lost, but I am stuck with chronic nerve pain.

Commentary eight
He can no longer pursue his career as a cameraman and relies on his wife for everything.

Chris
I have lost my career completely, my whole life was completely changed. I am unable to work at all due to the pain I am going through. Even now while I am talking to you I am in pain.

Commentary nine
In May last year the RAF signed a settlement agreement with him, but he still hasn’t been paid out. It’s now six years and counting

Chris
The payout is going to be something that we have waited for to get us through the situation of what I am dealing with now

Commentary Ten
Chris is one of thousands waiting, but the RAF is distracted because it’s at war with lawyers.

LINK
On the either side of the Road accident fund are lawyers – the plaintiff attorneys fighting for the best possible settlement for their clients, and the panel attorneys defending those claims on behalf of the RAF- and those fees are costing billions

Commentary Eleven
Every year treasury gives the RAF around R43 billion. It’s a sum total of the R2.07 cents we all pay every time we add a litre of fuel to our tanks.

Hennie
If a motorist has an average of about twenty five thousand kilometres per annum and petrol consumption of 10 kilometres per litre, then that equates to R432 per month
Masa
So that is how much people like you and me are paying?
Ya
Masa
So where is all the money?
Hennie
It’s gone into litigation, over 20 years

Commentary Eleven A
Last year R10 billion rand went to lawyers, even though 99% of RAF matters get settled on the steps of the court

Masa
Does the RAF spend too much on litigation?
Collins
Of course, unnecessary litigation. If you were settling 99% of the time, why would you want to litigate, even the panel attorneys will tell you they end up settling those matters anyway so why is there a need for a lawyer?

Commentary Twelve
Since 2014, the RAF has used about 100 different firms of panel attorneys. One of those was Maponya. Baitseng Rangata, Co-chairperson says they built their firm around the RAF’s needs

Baitseng
We have grown from a two directorship firm, we have gone beyond and we have built all of this, we have hired lawyers.

Commentary Thirteen
But shortly after he arrived, Letsoalo told the panel attorneys to take a hike

Masa
The panel attorneys say they were an easy target, is that something you would agree with?
Collins
No. It’s a simple thing you arrive, you find this organization going down, you ask yourself where the problem is, you see a hole- ten billion right? On the other side you see these guys bring the matters, on the other side these guys defend, you say I don’t want to litigate anymore, once you say that, who do you get rid of? The people you are using to litigate, it’s as simple as that. it’s a logical thing!

Commentary Fourteen
Maponya has been working on 6000 files for the RAF, now Letsoalo wants them back. Fine says Maponya, but pay us the outstanding R20 million you owe us. Letsoalo refused, so now Maponya are taking the RAF to court

LINK
Maponya’s application is bold – when the RAF refused to engage with them – they decided their only course of action was to go to court and apply to liquidate the fund


Baitseng
The RAF ideally it should not collapse, and we are in a position where the RAF is facing collapse, because the person who is sitting in the top seat has his eye on other things and I
I don’t have the confidence in the current CEO
MASA
What other things Baitseng?
Baitseng
Maponya is on the panel, you are going all out to ensure they don’t survive a day! And you go public and you say I am going to make your life difficult, I am going to make sure you return my files and I am not going to pay you! Why?
Masa
Maponya has 6000 of your files, the RAF wants the files back, Maponya says cool just pay us our R20 million and in between these legal disputes are actual claimants, victims of road accidents, wouldn’t it be better Collins to sit around a table instead of spending more money on litigation
Letsoalo
We sat with them, we explained what we wanted to do. When greed takes over I think certain people some brain cells move. I have said to you once you bring the file I am able to assess it, I don’t even know whether we owe that R20 million – actually we dispute that.

Commentary Fifteen
But Maponya says that in his answering affidavit, Letsoalo does not dispute that the RAF owes them R20 million. Transport minister Fikile Mbalula has also submitted affidavits

Masa
The minister says your claim is driven by financial interests?
Baitseng
You owe me you must pay me, you can qualify it whichever way you want. Maponya is a law firm, we have rendered a service, you must pay for that service

Commentary sixteen
The RAF is also engaged on another front, this time in a battle with the sheriff and plaintiff attorneys, who keep attaching their stuff.

Masa
How big a problem are the writs?
Collins
Its massive....
Masa
Give me examples
Collins
The chair I am sitting on

LINK
Everything from their chairs, to their bank accounts and even their phone lines were fair game


Commentary Seventeen
Between April 2019 and March last year, some lawyers jumped the queue and attached R3.9 billion rand of the funds money. So the RAF went to court to stop the attachments to give themselves breathing room, but that has meant many plaintiff attorneys cant’ get paid

Collins
When we close the holes, everyone is going to squeal. But that's something that we are hired to do and we're going to do it.

Commentary Eighteen
So the court battles rage on, and even Letsoalo himself is under fire. A group of plaintiff attorneys want the courts to reverse his appointment. They question his track record.

Masa
Another allegation is that you are vindictive and take reprisals against attorneys who challenge you in court. Is that you Collins?
Collins
It cannot be. And I take decisions that people don’t like- they make it about me simply because I refuse to accept certain things
Masa
Just one more allegation on these documents. You have been brought in as a turnaround guy. You have also mentioned your positive legacy, but that is not what they are saying. They say you’ve actually failed at turning around other organizations and you are going to fail again.
Collins
They must prove it. Look at my response to those allegations. Most of those allegations are false. They have no truth to them

Commentary Nineteen
Letsoalo has inherited a fund with liabilities that exceed its assets by R262 billion rand, that is running at a loss of about R11,3 billion per month. Now He wants to change the RAF act, substantially reduce legal fees and instead of paying lump sums, to pay out annuities instead.

Masa
As Carte blanche, we've done several stories on the road accident fund over the years. How long till you call us over and say, CB come back? We have turned things around and this is what we fixed and how we fixed it.
Collins
Well we said to South Africa in three years, we have spent the first year, uh Covid given another two years, we should bring you back here and you will see a different road accident fund.
Masa
One without defence attorneys,
Collins
of course, I mean, there's no future for defence attorneys in the model that we are taking going forward.

Commentary Twenty
Hopefully Letsoalo’s new model will work, because the debt of the RAF is an enormous risk to the economy, but the real solution to the RAF problem is simple. A drastic change of behaviour on our roads will dramatically reduce the killing and the maiming of South Africans.

THE END


PROMO ONE
The Road Accident fund is broke, its drowning in hundreds of thousands of claims, and now it’s at war with its former panel attorneys who want to liquidate the fund over unpaid bills.


PROMO TWO
Thousands of claimants to the Road Accident Fund have been waiting years for a settlement, but even that is no guarantee of payment, because the RAF has run out of road.


PROMO THREE
The debt of the Road Accident Fund is staggering, and is second only to Eskom as a risk to the fiscus. Now the new CEO is slashing costs and angering attorneys.

Baitseng You owe me you must pay me, you can qualify it whichever way you want. Maponya is a law firm, we have rendered a service, you must pay for that service Commentary sixteen The RAF is also engaged on another front, this time in a battle with the sheriff and plaintiff attorneys, who keep attaching their stuff. Masa How big a problem are the writs? Collins Its massive.... Masa Give me examples Collins The chair I am sitting on LINK Everything from their chairs, to their bank accounts and even their phone lines were fair game Commentary Seventeen Between April 2019 and March last year, some lawyers jumped the queue and attached R3.9 billion rand of the funds money. So the RAF went to court to stop the attachments to give themselves breathing room, but that has meant many plaintiff attorneys cant’ get paid Collins When we close the holes, everyone is going to squeal. But that's something that we are hired to do and we're going to do it. Commentary Eighteen So the court battles rage on, and even Letsoalo himself is under fire. A group of plaintiff attorneys want the courts to reverse his appointment. They question his track record. Masa Another allegation is that you are vindictive and take reprisals against attorneys who challenge you in court. Is that you Collins? Collins It cannot be. And I take decisions that people don’t like- they make it about me simply because I refuse to accept certain things Masa Just one more allegation on these documents. You have been brought in as a turnaround guy. You have also mentioned your positive legacy, but that is not what they are saying. They say you’ve actually failed at turning around other organizations and you are going to fail again. Collins They must prove it. Look at my response to those allegations. Most of those allegations are false. They have no truth to them Commentary Nineteen Letsoalo has inherited a fund with liabilities that exceed its assets by R262 billion rand, that is running at a loss of about R11,3 billion per month. Now He wants to change the RAF act, substantially reduce legal fees and instead of paying lump sums, to pay out annuities instead. Masa As Carte blanche, we've done several stories on the road accident fund over the years. How long till you call us over and say, CB come back? We have turned things around and this is what we fixed and how we fixed it. Collins Well we said to South Africa in three years, we have spent the first year, uh Covid given another two years, we should bring you back here and you will see a different road accident fund. Masa One without defence attorneys, Collins of course, I mean, there's no future for defence attorneys in the model that we are taking going forward. Commentary Twenty Hopefully Letsoalo’s new model will work, because the debt of the RAF is an enormous risk to the economy, but the real solution to the RAF problem is simple. A drastic change of behaviour on our roads will dramatically reduce the killing and the maiming of South Africans. THE END PROMO ONE The Road Accident fund is broke, its drowning in hundreds of thousands of claims, and now it’s at war with its former panel attorneys who want to liquidate the fund over unpaid bills. PROMO TWO Thousands of claimants to the Road Accident Fund have been waiting years for a settlement, but even that is no guarantee of payment, because the RAF has run out of road. PROMO THREE The debt of the Road Accident Fund is staggering, and is second only to Eskom as a risk to the fiscus. Now the new CEO is slashing costs and angering attorneys. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The RAF has run out of road. What can save it and who is at the helm
metadata.Unique Selling Point: All the information in our story is a matter of court record. ITs contentious, its important and its about to fall over and Maponya are prepared to speak to Carte Blanche
metadata.Summary: In the final months of 2020, a flurry of legal action around the RAF was taking place. Attorneys are suing the RAF, the RAF was going to court to prevent the attorneys from removing its furniture, its bank account and even the fuel levy on which it depends, and another firm of former panel attorneys, Maponya prepared lengthy documents to apply to wind up the RAF but put their application on hold till January this year. There were judgements and appeals, but now its 2021 when the rubber will hit the road for the RAF and those in the know say it could implode
metadata.Further information: Every year there are a million accidents, 13 000 deaths and more than 262 000 injures. That translates into 100 000 personal claims against the RAF every year, but only 47% are finalized which means that over 53 000 claims are carried over to the following year. Now add those to the 245 000 claims that are still outstanding, not enough staff to process the claims and some voracious plaintiff attorneys into the mix and its easy to see how an implosion can happen. And even as lawyers and sheriffs fight the RAF, the RAF itself has taken its own bank to court to prevent it from handing out money when court orders from frustrated attorneys trying to get claims paid for their clients, attach its bank accounts. But there is more – in an application launched by plaintiff attorney Kabelo Malau, he asks the court to find the recent appointment of the new CEO Collins Letsoalo irrational. He sets out clearly the history of Letsoalo at the RTMC and PRASA, and its an unflattering picture. ( Malau wont go on the record but we can find a way to reflect what is in the papers. In December the RAF managed to get a rule Nisi – an interdict that expires after a certain time frame – to give it 180 days ( 6 months) of breathing room in which no sheriff or plaintiff attorney can attach its bank account or its computers or its chairs. It seems hard to believe but its become almost standard practice for plaintiff attorneys to get a court order to get payment and attach whatever they can if the RAF doesn’t settle their long overdue claims. There are over 5000 attachments pending- speak to PIPLA – the plaintiff attorneys association and they will tell you that at one legal firm alone there is R100 million in writs – just waiting for a window to attach the ABSA bank account. The urgent application by the CEO of the RAF was granted in November last year, but its not permanent. That case will go back to court next month, but in the meantime – the CEO’s affidavit sets out the train wreck that is the RAF’s financial situation. The CEO says the RAF is insolvent and he highlights very specifically the exact amounts – and they are eye watering. According to the minister and the CEO a massive deficit has worsened dramatically over the past five years. A the end of 2018 it was R26.4 billion, by end 2019 it was R55.8 billion and now they are staring down a R260 billion deficit. But, Letsoalo tells the courts he has a five year plan to turn the RAF around. Don’t hold your breath, so far no one has managed to pull the RAF right, and the billions it owes now means that the RAF is the second biggest risk to the country’s balance sheet after Eskom. And then there is the pandemic. For every litre of petrol we buy the RAF takes just over R2-00 of that. If you are an average motorist in SA you are paying roughly R400 per month for the benefit of the RAF. But if you are ever a victim of a serious MVA injury, you could wait up to seven years for your money. And lockdown last year didn’t help – they are R7 billion rand down. Maponya can prove they are owed R20 million rand for work already done, but they say that at the start of lockdown the RAF pulled the rug from under them, and demanded their files. This is part of the new strategy of the CEO – get rid of the panel attorneys that are there to help protect RAF funds from over inflated claims by plaintiff attorney. Its been almost a year and Maponya’s Baitseng Rangata – chairperson of the board has run out of patience. Their application is ready for the court role. It could be precedent setting, it could be disastrous. The minister who has opposed the application says it is self- serving and incompetent in law, as only parliament can decide what to do with the RAF – not Maponya application using the companies act to liquidate the fund. So does the RAF have a future in its current form, or is it time to look at another way of doing things? Certainly the way that both the RAF and attorneys are operating has become almost farcical, except that its tragic, because those injured in life changing accidents, the stretched South African motorist, and the fiscus are all the worse off, as long as this sorry saga continues. Carte Blanche navigates our viewers through this morass, we speak to Maponya, and Professor Hennie Klopper and others, to bring you a crisp and concise overview of a fund that is supposed to be an asset for South Africa but instead has become its second biggest liability after Eskom.
